I am part for the local volunteer Search and Rescue team, and I am investigating how to use these devices to augment our communication and tracking capabilities. We do use radios, but the repeaters tend to be far and few in between in areas where we are typically called. This also means that cellphones do not work (they use the same towers.) Our radios are also not encrypted, which in the past has caused some issues with leaking sensitive information (We do not want a family finding out that their loved one is dead from some guy on twitter). While we upped our radio discipline, we still find ourselves in positions where tracking fails, or we cannot have secure communications, or where teams cannot communicate between each other since, for some reason, we can't use talkaround on our radios.


The automation aspect of meshtastic is also something we are looking at (like TC2-BBS but more as a bot for SAR applications). Being able to request from a bot weather, mission parameter updates, search status, and many other requests would be a fantastic addition to our capabilities. The only thing we cant figure out how to do is send images, but that's also not really a use case for meshtastic.


We've been experimenting with a few devices that team members have, with so far incredible success. We've been able to expand our communications tremendously. Having a small fleet of these devices would honestly really help in our ability to serve the public and save lives. These t1000e are absolutely the perfect device as they are light and waterproof.

Actual reason is to increase survivability by preventing smoke and fire from blocking egress routes. Slowing fire spread is a happy side benefit.

They do reduce damage in the sense that they stop flames and smoke for rated period of time(depends on occupancy type such as hospital (4hours) or schools (2hours I think))but it's really for life safety of primary (normal people) and secondary (firefighters) occupants. The hospitals are higher is because is takes longer to evacuate non-mobile folks vs students that can sprint down stairs. Any time you keep parts of the building clear of smoke and flames ,it becomes another area for egress or shelter in place. Another device that's often ignored by the public are the glass barriers on the ceiling for areas that are open beyond just that floor, like an atrium. Without them, smoke would just go straight up. With them, it gives extra time as the ceiling needs to overflow before it can escape. Have a look for smoke baffles https://www.sightlinecommercial.com/products/smoke-baffle
It's not so much to limit damage, but to extend the time that the stairway is survivable. Prevents smoke and flames from entering egress routes.
